_doc: T3.5 (D-035, d018). The eight-need ladder is frozen (D-018 3); BOUND grows by milestone. M2 bound Sustenance alone; M3/T3.5 binds Sustenance, Shelter and Comfort (T3.8: Shelter now reads the housing stock via source=housingStock; Sustenance/Comfort stay basket-bound). An UNBOUND need contributes EXACTLY nothing whatever its weight says (T2.6 zero-effect gate). varietyWeight is the D-035-A concentration coefficient INSIDE the satisfaction equation - 0 means the need has no diversity dimension (Shelter: two dwellings' worth of timber is not a more varied roof).

needs.name: Dignity/Liberty
needs._doc: M5 R2b - D-035-D (taxation -> Dignity is DIRECT): bound with source taxBurden, satisfaction = 1 - the settlement's effective tax rate (declared rate x administrative reach, Governance.EffectiveTaxRate) on PREV. The carrier is the tax instrument itself; no basket serves it (the loader refuses one). Publishes nothing in a config with no governance section (no instrument, no carrier). Liberty's other carriers (garrisons, censorship - D-035-C path 6) are later institutions.

aggregation._doc: D-035-B. CES over BOUND needs with substitution elasticity sigma < 1, replacing d018:52's weighted sum. rho = (sigma-1)/sigma < 0 makes needs genuine COMPLEMENTS: surplus comfort cannot buy off absent shelter. sigma 0.5 (rho = -1, the weighted harmonic mean) is the round value squarely inside the non-compensatory regime and far from the sigma=1 Cobb-Douglas degeneration. satisfactionFloor states how bad ONE need at zero is allowed to make the aggregate: at exactly zero the CES limit is 0 regardless of everything else - true in the limit, but it would make a world with nothing indistinguishable from a world with almost nothing and every settlement equally, maximally aggrieved. 0.05 says total deprivation of a single need is very bad, not infinitely bad. It is a MECHANISM PARAMETER, not a guard - raising it weakens non-compensation continuously - and the D-035-B acceptance ceiling is DERIVED from it, never chosen alongside it.
aggregation._tierADoc: d018:46, retained unchanged by D-035-B and applied to the WEIGHTS before aggregation. Below tierAFloor a gate need (Sustenance/Shelter/Safety) scales superlinearly and collapses upper-need weights toward zero: a starving intelligentsia riots over bread, not press freedom. tierAFloor 0.5 = 'half-fed is where the ladder inverts'; tierAGain 3.0 = a wholly unmet gate need weighs 4x its normal weight; tierACollapse 1.0 = upper weights fall linearly in gate severity toward zero.

baskets._doc: D-035-C path 1 (SHARED SATISFIER) and path 2 (SHARED BUDGET) made data. One entry per (class, need, good); perPersonYear is a per-sim-year rate integrated with dtYears (law 3), never a per-turn amount. FOOD entries are denominated in PERSON-YEAR-EQUIVALENTS of nutrition, the D-015 convention grain already carries: a class's food entries sum to 1.0 by construction, so the basket changes WHAT is eaten and never how much nutrition a person needs. Peasants eat a staple diet; artisans, with income and a market, eat measurably more livestock and fish - the T3.5 class-differentiation requirement IS this table, not a coefficient bolted on afterwards. SUBSTITUTION: unmet non-staple food demand falls back on the staple (grain), because a household short of fish eats more bread rather than going hungry while grain sits in the store. Monotony is then paid for in the D-035-A variety term rather than in calories, which is exactly the director's rationale - a settlement that can feed itself entirely on grain still has a reason to import fish. SHELTER left this table at T3.8: it now reads the housing STOCK (needs[].source = housingStock) exactly as the old stand-in's own doc anticipated; the material draw moved into HousingSystem's build/maintenance sinks. TUNE, all of it.
baskets._docMerchants: T4.11. Merchants sit one step further from the staple than artisans (grain 0.74 vs 0.78) and correspondingly higher on livestock and fish. The reasoning is the same one the table already encodes for artisans - income and market access change WHAT is eaten, never how much nutrition a person needs, and the food entries still sum to exactly 1.0 by construction - with the additional point that a merchant's living IS market access: the class that moves livestock and fish between settlements is the least likely of the three to be eating only what grows in its own catchment. Comfort is likewise slightly above artisans (pottery 0.06, cloth 0.10 vs 0.05/0.08). TUNE, like every other row here. The mechanical consequence to be aware of is that merchants import MORE and are therefore hit harder when trade stops - which is the correct coupling for a trading class and not a penalty bolted on.

unrest._doc: M5 R2b - D-021 UNREST-LITE (the brake ships with the M5 gas pedal, the tax). A settlement's population-weighted grievance G (PREV) expresses as PROTEST p = clamp((G - protestOnsetGrievance) / (uprisingGrievance - protestOnsetGrievance), 0, 1). Consequences, each growing with p and exactly inert at p = 0: realised production x (1 - protestOutputDragMax x p x r), r the settlement's effective tax rate (d009 'protest (production drag)': the levied effort withheld - its carrier is the levy, so an untaxed, e.g. famine-driven, protest drags nothing and hunger cannot feed on itself through it); grievance decay rate + protestDischargePerYear x p (D-021 valve 1, expression discharges pressure, so episodes END); at p = 1 the settlement rises and throws off its ruler (RevoltSystem). ALL TUNE. protestOnsetGrievance 15 and uprisingGrievance 50 are on the scale of the LEVY'S grievance (State.Unrest.TaxGrievance: the stock x the share of the aggregate shortfall that lifting the levy would close - zero wherever no tax is felt, so pottery- or diet-driven grievance never ignites a protest against a ruler who takes nothing). CHOSEN WITHIN A MEASURED FRAME (founded seed-42 world, 300 turns, the seat's levy grievance; docs/m5-integration-coherence-matrix.md section 6): a 40 % levy (the AI ceiling) plateaus at 6.7-7.6 and the onset is twice that, so normal taxation never protests; a 70 % levy plateaus at 20-22 (mild protest, p ~0.15-0.19); a 99 % levy climbs to 47-54 and the uprising sits inside that band, so sustained near-total exaction ends in a rising and nothing short of it does. protestOutputDragMax 0.5: CHOSEN - at full protest under a total levy a settlement works at half its output; framed by production.toolYieldBonusMax 0.3 and governance.taxExtractionResponseMax 0.3, so full protest takes back more than full extraction gives (1.3 x 0.5 < 1). protestDischargePerYear 0.005: CHOSEN - at full protest the stock vents at an extra 0.5 %/yr on top of base and generational decay (~1.5 %/yr measured), which is what ends an episode once its cause stops while staying weak enough that sustained total exaction still reaches the rising (a stronger valve - 0.05 was measured - pins the stock below the rising for any levy, so the brake would never bite).

varietyStandard._doc: T3.5b item 2 (director ruling): the FIXED NUTRITIONAL DIVERSITY STANDARD - the reference composition of a varied pre-modern agrarian diet, independent of both what a class declares and what it receives. DERIVED, not fitted (docs/t3.5b-derivations.md section 2): staple 0.70 / animal-and-fish 0.20 / other 0.10, from diet-history reconstruction anchored to ADR-013's own 'cereals 75% of calories' chain. H* = 0.70^2+0.20^2+0.10^2 = 0.54. The variety factor penalises only EXCESS concentration beyond H*: a diet at or below it takes no penalty (full satisfaction expressible); a grain-only diet (H = 1) takes the full varietyWeight penalty, so the D-035-A reason to trade survives. NOTE the shipped baskets are MORE concentrated than this standard (peasant food H = 0.8152) - a fully supplied frontier grain economy scores 0.910 on Sustenance, not 1.0, which is the honest reading: its diet is monotonous by the standard of a good pre-modern diet, and imports are how it closes the gap.
